model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: The agent definition's output template names claude-fable-5. This evaluation was actually produced by Opus 5 (1M context), model id claude-opus-5[1m], running as a Claude Code subagent. Both model.name and model.evaluator_model record the true runtime identity rather than the template default, so reproduction claims are attributed to the model that made this judgement.

issues_detected.description: Version ordering is not monotonic. version is "2.0" for the June 2026 release, but version_access lists the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases at version 2.1, so the newest release carries a lower version number than two of its predecessors. The citation independently says "V2". Either the release numbering genuinely resets per Dataverse major version and needs a stated explanation, or one of the version values is wrong.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the versioning scheme explicitly in version_access, or correct the June 2026 version so it sorts after the October 2025 release.

issues_detected.description: Two different project end dates. updates.update_details says the dataset is augmented "through the end of the project in November 2026", while funders[0].notes records an NIH RePORTER project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31. A user planning around the last quarterly update cannot tell which end date governs.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reconcile the two dates, or note that the award period and the project's data-release commitment differ and say why.

issues_detected.description: preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools document the MuSIC cell-map construction pipeline end to end (node2vec PPI embedding, DenseNet-121 image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF community detection, GPT-4/GSAI assembly naming), but known_limitations and discouraged_uses state that this release does not contain predicted cell maps. The documented processing therefore describes a downstream pipeline whose products are absent from the distributed files. source_caveats partially concedes this by noting that MuSIC method text was drawn from a distinct U2OS publication.
issues_detected.recommendation: Separate processing actually applied to the released archives from the roadmap pipeline that will produce future cell maps, so a reuser knows which steps the shipped files have been through.

issues_detected.description: cleaning_strategies contains a single entry stating that CRISPR screen data "were reported as undergoing quality control at the time of the CM4AI preprint". That describes a state at an earlier point in time, not a cleaning procedure applied to the released data, and does not say what quality control consisted of or whether it completed.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the quality-control criteria applied to the released Perturb-seq archives and their outcome, or mark the slot as not yet documented.

issues_detected.description: known_biases records only representation_bias, while known_limitations separately records that SEC-MS, immunofluorescence, and CRISPRi Perturb-seq interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets, and sampling_strategies records a targeted protein-level selection of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes. Those are selection and measurement biases documented as limitations rather than categorized as biases, so the bias taxonomy understates what the record itself knows.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add selection_bias for the targeted protein panel and measurement_bias for antibody- and assay-dependent coverage, with AIO mappings.

issues_detected.description: Grant identifiers are correct in form but are carried as free prose inside funders[].notes rather than in a structured award field. Machine extraction of 1OT2OD032742-01 and 5U54HG012513-02 therefore requires parsing English sentences.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate a structured grant/award number field alongside grantor, keeping the RePORTER detail in notes.

issues_detected.description: File sizes are recorded only as human-readable strings inside file_collections[].description ("Listed at 3.8 GB"), and total_size_bytes is omitted. source_caveats justifies this: the bundle states no exact byte counts. The information is present but not machine-comparable, and file_collections.total_bytes is unused.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record approximate byte counts in file_collections[].total_bytes and mark them as derived from displayed values.

issues_detected.description: raw_sources and external_resources name the external repositories that hold the component raw data (MassIVE, Sequence Read Archive via NCBI BioProject, Figshare) but give no accession identifiers for any of them. Cross-dataset linking to those depositions is therefore not actionable from this record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add MassIVE accessions, the BioProject id, and the Figshare DOI where the bundle states them.

issues_detected.description: created_on is 2025-02-27, sixteen months before issued (2026-06-17), and five immunofluorescence archives carry a publication date of 2026-07-15, after the release's own issue date. The record anticipates both: source_caveats states the Dataverse creation date is carried unchanged across four release records and is unlikely to be release-specific, and the format notes explain the later image publication. Documented rather than contradictory, but a consumer sorting on created_on will mis-order the releases.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the caveat and consider omitting created_on entirely, since the record already argues it is not specific to this release.

semantic_insights: DOI prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse prefix and agrees with publisher ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia) and with the citation text naming University of Virginia Dataverse. Three independent fields corroborate one another.

Grant identifiers follow NIH structure correctly: 1OT2OD032742-01 parses as application type 1, activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032742, support year 01, and 5U54HG012513-02 as a U54 center award at NHGRI, which is the correct institute for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center.
Related-work DOIs both carry the 10.1101 bioRxiv prefix, consistent with their description as preprints.

Cell lines carry Cellosaurus RRIDs in valid form (RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468, RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J). CVCL is the correct namespace for cell lines; the rubric's SCR_/AB_ patterns do not apply to this resource type.

total_file_count is 10 and file_collections contains exactly 10 entries, each with an MD5 checksum, a publication date, and a displayed size. The internal count is self-consistent and the checksums are a genuine integrity signal.

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=false is well supported rather than merely asserted: direct_collection records is_direct=false with commercially available de-identified lines, confidential_elements and sensitive_elements both declare presence=false with reasons, and regulatory_restrictions sets hipaa_compliant=not_applicable. The ethics claims are internally coherent for in vitro cell-line data.

The record still documents ethical review, a named Data Access Committee, and IP restrictions despite claiming no human subjects, which is the right posture for human-derived material and exceeds what the no-human-subjects declaration would require.

Prohibited-use reasoning is traceable: the non-commercial prohibition cites CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and names the same rights holders (UCSD, Stanford, UCSF) that ip_restrictions attributes copyright to, and UCSD and UCSF both fall under the Regents of the University of California as stated.

source_caveats does real epistemic work: it declines to attribute project-level aggregate counts (1,374 interactions, 53,788 images, 21.4 TB) to this release, separates a U2OS cell map publication from the CM4AI releases, and explains three specific omissions (total_size_bytes, last_updated_on, collection_timeframes) by pointing to what the bundle does not state.

Two source conflicts are surfaced rather than silently resolved: an immunofluorescence protein count of 563 versus 464 across release pages, and an affiliation conflict for one creator between the release metadata and the preprint. Both name the losing value and the ranking rule applied.
Ontology CURIEs appear where the schema expects them (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19 and :63, B2AI_TOPIC:12, :15, :26), alongside ORCID, ROR, and DOI CURIEs, giving the record consistent identifier discipline.
related_datasets uses typed relationships (is_new_version_of, is_described_by, is_referenced_by) with DOI targets, which is the correct semantic shape for a versioned quarterly release series.

correctness_validations.doi_registrar_match: valid — 10.18130 (University of Virginia Dataverse) agrees with publisher and citation
correctness_validations.rrid_format: valid — Cellosaurus CVCL namespace, correct for cell lines
correctness_validations.checksum_presence: present — MD5 on all 10 file collections

human_subjects.evidence: description names human cell lines and human induced pluripotent stem cells; keywords include 'induced pluripotent stem cell', 'iPSC', 'KOLF2.1J', 'MDA-MB-468'. collection_mechanisms (Q12) describes laboratory assays with no participant recruitment. No human participants, patients, or clinical research are referenced. The material is human-derived but the research is in vitro, which makes the condition genuinely borderline; per the ambiguity rule the default is applicable, and Q8 and Q15 are scored on what the record documents.

datasets_shared.evidence: distribution_formats populated with ZIP Archive (application/zip) and RO-Crate, with access_urls to the University of Virginia Dataverse persistent identifier page; license_and_use_terms grants CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 reuse.

software_tools_output.evidence: external_resources (Q14 field) names the Cell Mapping Toolkit at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with documentation at cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, the FAIRSCAPE framework at fairscape.github.io under MIT License, and the Integrative Modeling Platform at integrativemodeling.org. Code repositories are referenced, so Q11 is applicable without relying on Q11's own fields.

collection_and_shared.evidence: acquisition_methods (4), collection_mechanisms (4), data_collectors (3), and raw_data_sources (2) are all populated, and the datasets-shared condition above is met.

publication_and_shared.evidence: citation carries a full Dataverse citation with DOI; related_datasets includes is_described_by doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and is_referenced_by doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734; datasets-shared condition met.

questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated
questions.score_label: Very good — roughly 80% of the named fields covered
questions.evidence: Present: id (doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C), title, description (~1,700 chars), keywords (30), license_and_use_terms (full CC BY-NC-SA text plus data_use_permission and contact), doi, page (https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/), creators (45 with affiliations), purposes (4), instances (3). Substituted rather than named: 'resources' is expressed as external_resources (11 entries); 'parent_datasets' is expressed as related_datasets with four is_new_version_of links. Genuinely absent: variables, regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level.
questions.quality_note: Ten of fourteen named fields are populated exactly, and two more are covered by adjacent slots carrying the same information. The real gaps are variable-level description and a confidentiality classification enum; the latter matters because the record does declare confidential_elements_present=false elsewhere, so only the standardized level is missing.

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields have meaningful content length
questions.score_label: >200 chars
questions.evidence: description runs approximately 1,700 characters and names each modality with its cell line and treatment condition. purposes has four responses averaging roughly 230 characters each, from 'deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data' through 'visible machine learning systems ... built directly on knowledge maps'.
questions.quality_note: Well past the top threshold, and the length is substantive rather than padded: the description enumerates which assays cover which cell states, which is the fact a reuser needs first.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords describing topic coverage
questions.score_label: ≥8 keywords
questions.evidence: 30 unique keywords spanning assay names (AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, scRNAseq, size exclusion chromatography), biological material (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, iPSC, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte), perturbagens (paclitaxel, vorinostat, CRISPR/Cas9), and program context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI, AI, machine learning).
questions.quality_note: Nearly four times the top threshold, and the set covers assay, material, perturbagen, and program axes rather than repeating one axis. Includes both expanded and abbreviated forms of the same term (single-cell RNA sequencing / scRNAseq), which helps discovery.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of distribution formats and file type diversity
questions.score_label: 2–3 file types
questions.evidence: distribution_formats lists two: 'ZIP Archive' with media_type application/zip, and 'RO-Crate'. file_collections enumerates 10 archives, every one with compression: zip. total_file_count: 10.
questions.quality_note: Enumeration is excellent (all ten archives named, sized, dated, and checksummed) but format variety is thin at the distribution layer. The underlying data are genuinely multi-modal, which description and keywords establish, yet the formats inside the archives (confocal image format, mass-spectrometry output format, sequence format) are never named, so a reuser cannot tell what they will find after unzipping. Two format entries places this at the middle band.

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or instance count metadata
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: Per-file sizes appear in every file_collections description: 113.3 KB, 135.8 KB, 3.8 GB, 4.6 GB, 4.2 GB, 171.8 KB, 93.9 KB, 30.2 KB, 73.3 KB, 1.1 MB. Instance counts appear as 464 proteins of interest imaged per treatment condition and 11,739 targeted genes in the CRISPRi atlas. subsets enumerates seven subpopulations.
questions.quality_note: Passes on both size and count evidence. The semantic weakness is placement, not absence: sizes are prose inside descriptions rather than file_collections.total_bytes, and total_size_bytes is omitted with a stated reason (the bundle gives no byte values). The record also notes that the Perturb-seq entry states targeted genes but not profiled cells, which is an honest scoping of what the count covers.

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; publisher: ROR:0153tk833; access_urls includes the Dataverse persistentId landing page. Cell lines carry RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3; 38 creators carry ORCIDs.
questions.quality_note: Passes decisively. The DOI prefix, the publisher ROR, and the citation's repository name all independently point to the University of Virginia, so the persistent identifier is corroborated rather than merely present.

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Funding sources, grants, creator affiliations, institutional sponsors
questions.score_label: Funders with grants + creators with affiliations
questions.evidence: Three funders: NIH award 1OT2OD032742-01 with RePORTER detail (core project OT2OD032742, application ID 11211616, PI Trey Ideker, UCSD, period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, FY2025 amount 5,289,382); NIH award 5U54HG012513-02 for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center; and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia. All 45 creators carry affiliations, 38 carry ORCIDs, and five carry ROR-identified University of Virginia affiliations.
questions.quality_note: Top band on both halves of the criterion. Award numbers validate against NIH structure and the institute codes are the right ones for this program. The one deduction I considered but did not take is that award numbers live in free-text notes rather than a structured grant field, which is logged as a low-severity correctness issue rather than a scoring penalty because the content itself is complete and specific.

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.applicability_evidence: description and keywords reference human cell lines and human induced pluripotent stem cells, and the material derives from identifiable human donors, but collection_mechanisms (Q12) describes only laboratory assays with no participant recruitment. Borderline, so the ambiguity rule applies and the question is scored on what is documented.
questions.description: Comprehensive ethics coverage
questions.score_label: Very good — comprehensive for the data type, with structured slots unused
questions.evidence: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false with a note recording 'Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No' and stating both lines were ethically sourced (MDA-MB-468 from ATCC, KOLF2.1J from HipSci via a simple MTA for not-for-profit access). is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false with the reasoning that the data are non-clinical and cannot be matched to a human subject with current knowledge. Two ethical_reviews entries with named contacts (Vardit Ravitsky, Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon) and their institutional emails. data_governance names the CM4AI Data Access Committee, its contact, its access review process, and stewardship roles. confidential_elements and sensitive_elements both declare presence=false with reasons. regulatory_restrictions sets hipaa_compliant: not_applicable and records FDA Regulated: No.
questions.quality_note: The ethics story is coherent and each claim is supported rather than asserted: the no-human-subjects declaration is backed by direct_collection.is_direct=false and the commercial provenance of both lines. Held below 5 for two reasons. First, the structured slots that would carry the remaining protections are unused: data_protection_impacts, participant_privacy, informed_consent, participant_compensation, and at_risk_populations are all absent rather than explicitly marked not applicable, so a reader cannot distinguish 'not relevant here' from 'not documented'. Second, the donor consent chain that does exist for cell-line material is only gestured at through the phrase 'ethically sourced' and the HipSci MTA, with no consent terms stated.

questions.name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
questions.description: Access policy, license, IP restrictions, regulatory restrictions, confidentiality level
questions.score_label: License + restrictions + confidentiality classification
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms gives the full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 obligations (credit, license link, changes indicated, non-commercial, share-alike), sets data_use_permission: no_commercial_use, and names a contact. ip_restrictions attributes copyright to the Regents of the University of California except spatial proteomics raw images, which are copyright the Board of Trustees of Stanford, and states that commercial use requires negotiation with UCSD, Stanford, and/or UCSF depending on the data package. regulatory_restrictions records FDA Regulated: No, hipaa_compliant: not_applicable, and a governance committee contact. data_governance describes the Data Access Committee and its supervision of dissemination and dual licensing.
questions.quality_note: All three components of the top band are present, and the IP layer is unusually precise: it distinguishes rights holders per data package rather than making a single blanket claim, which is what a commercial reuser would actually need. The one missing element is the regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level enum, but the equivalent classification is carried by confidential_elements_present=false and sensitive_elements_present=false with reasons, so the information is not absent.

questions.name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated with access_urls to the Dataverse landing page and a reuse-permitting CC BY-NC-SA license.
questions.description: Standard formats, ontologies, schema conformance, cross-platform linkage, integration capability
questions.score_label: Standard formats + schema/ontology compliance + integration capability
questions.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. distribution_formats includes RO-Crate with the note that output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata using the FAIRSCAPE framework. Ontology CURIEs appear on instances (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:63, B2AI_TOPIC:12, B2AI_TOPIC:15, B2AI_TOPIC:26). Cross-dataset linkage uses typed relationships in related_datasets (is_new_version_of ×4, is_described_by, is_referenced_by) with DOI targets, plus identifier discipline via ORCID, ROR, DOI, and Cellosaurus RRID CURIEs.
questions.quality_note: Top band on all three components. RO-Crate plus FAIRSCAPE is a domain-recognized AI-readiness packaging choice rather than a generic format claim, and the schema and class are both declared, which makes the record itself machine-validatable. Two frictions keep this from being frictionless in practice and are logged as low-severity issues rather than a score deduction: the outer distribution is opaque ZIP with no internal formats named, and the external repository depositions (MassIVE, SRA BioProject, Figshare) are named without accession identifiers, so the cross-platform links are directional rather than resolvable.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.applicability_evidence: external_resources (a Q14 field) names three code repositories as project outputs: the Cell Mapping Toolkit at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with readthedocs documentation, FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io under the MIT License, and the Integrative Modeling Platform at http://integrativemodeling.org. Determined without reference to Q11's own fields.
questions.description: Preprocessing, cleaning, labeling strategies and software tooling
questions.score_label: Very good — comprehensive strategies, no versions
questions.evidence: preprocessing_strategies gives four ordered stages: node2vec dimensionality reduction of downloaded PPI networks into a PPI embedding; a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model producing an image embedding; contrastive deep learning integration into per-protein co-embeddings that can reconstruct the originals with minimal loss; and community detection on all-by-all co-embedding similarities yielding the hierarchy. machine_annotation_tools names node2vec, DenseNet-121, GPT-4, and HiDeF, each with a description of its role. labeling_strategies describes two-pronged annotation, aligning maps to Gene Ontology and Reactome and naming assemblies via a large language model, with data_annotation_platform 'Gene Set AI (GSAI) pipeline guiding the GPT-4 model'. cleaning_strategies has one entry.
questions.quality_note: Strategy coverage is genuinely comprehensive and the tool descriptions explain what each model contributes rather than just naming it. Held at 4 by three gaps. No version or release identifier appears for any tool, and GPT-4 in particular is a moving target where the version materially changes annotation output. Tool URLs live in external_resources rather than beside the tools, so the link between DenseNet-121 or HiDeF and its implementation is left to the reader. imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation, and annotation_analyses are unused. Separately, the scope mismatch flagged in the semantic analysis applies here: these strategies describe the cell-map pipeline whose outputs this release explicitly excludes.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.applicability_evidence: Collection fields populated (acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors, raw_data_sources) and the datasets-shared condition is met.
questions.description: Collection mechanisms, acquisition methods, collectors, timeframes
questions.score_label: Very good — methods and collectors detailed, timeframes absent
questions.evidence: acquisition_methods has four entries with was_directly_observed flags, including immunofluorescence detail at channel level (DAPI blue for nuclei, calreticulin yellow for endoplasmic reticulum, tubulin red for microtubules, target protein green) with was_validated_verified: true and a note that antibody quality was scored under a standard Human Protein Atlas protocol. collection_mechanisms adds instrument and protocol specifics: automated fixation and permeabilization on a pipetting robot, a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors at 6 guide RNAs per gene in inducible dCas9 lines, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit. data_collectors names three laboratories with role: academic_institution. raw_data_sources names two laboratory deposition archives.
questions.quality_note: The protocol detail is at the level a methods section would carry, with named instruments, reagents, channel assignments, and guide-RNA density, and each modality is attributed to a specific laboratory. The single missing component of the top band is collection_timeframes, which is omitted with an explicit justification in source_caveats that no collection start or end date is stated in the bundle. An honest omission, but the reuser still cannot date the experiments.

questions.name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
questions.applicability_evidence: Collection fields populated and datasets-shared condition met.
questions.description: Version information, access, errata, update plans, sustainability
questions.score_label: Very good — full sustainability documentation, version numbering inconsistent
questions.evidence: version: '2.0'. version_access.versions_available enumerates five releases (May 2024, March 2025 at 1.4, June 2025 at 2.1, October 2025 at 2.1, June 2026) and states that version history is maintained in the University of Virginia Dataverse, with latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C. updates records quarterly frequency through the end of the project. maintainers lists three named people with institutions, roles, and contact emails. retention_limit records long-term preservation in the UVA Dataverse 'supported by committed institutional funds'. related_datasets links all four prior releases by DOI with is_new_version_of.
questions.quality_note: Every sustainability component the rubric names is present: a DOI as persistent identifier, an institutional repository with a stated preservation commitment backed by funds, a governance structure via the Data Access Committee, and a maintenance cadence with named maintainers. The deduction is for the version-ordering failure logged in the semantic analysis: this release is numbered 2.0 while two earlier releases are listed at 2.1, so version sorting misorders the series. errata is also unused, which matters for a release series that has already superseded four predecessors and corrected at least one count (563 to 464 proteins imaged).

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.applicability_evidence: citation is populated with a formal dataset citation carrying a DOI, and datasets-shared condition met.
questions.description: Formal citations and DOI-linked external references
questions.score_label: Multiple references and dataset citation
questions.evidence: citation is a complete Dataverse-style citation naming 45 authors, year 2026, title, https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, repository, and version V2. related_datasets carries is_described_by doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 (the CM4AI preprint) and is_referenced_by doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 (A Perturbation Cell Atlas of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells), plus four prior-release DOIs. external_resources has eleven entries including the project portal, the Cell Mapping Toolkit repository and documentation, FAIRSCAPE, and the Integrative Modeling Platform.
questions.quality_note: Top band comfortably: a formal, complete dataset citation plus two DOI-identified publications attached with the correct relationship types plus a substantial external resource set. The distinction between is_described_by for the paper describing this data and is_referenced_by for the paper the Perturb-seq component draws on is semantically correct rather than a blanket 'related' label.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.applicability_evidence: Same borderline determination as Q8: description and keywords reference human-derived cell lines and iPSCs, while no human participants are recruited. Scored on what is documented per the ambiguity rule.
questions.description: Human subjects, demographic diversity, subgroup detail
questions.score_label: Very good — detailed subgroup characterization, no participant cohort
questions.evidence: subsets enumerates seven populations with stable ids, names, descriptions, and is_subpopulation: true, covering MDA-MB-468 untreated, paclitaxel-treated, and vorinostat-treated, plus KOLF2.1J undifferentiated, NPC, neuron, and cardiomyocyte, each stating which assays cover it. subpopulations gives identification by cell type and treatment condition and a distribution statement (464 proteins imaged per MDA-MB-468 condition; SEC-MS across all seven; AP-MS on treated MDA-MB-468 only). instances describes three instance types with substrate and topic CURIEs. Donor characteristics appear in sampling_strategies.source_data: MDA-MB-468 from a pleural effusion metastasis of a 51-year-old Black woman with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, and KOLF2.1J from a healthy male Northern European donor.
questions.quality_note: Subgroup characterization is thorough and, importantly, states assay coverage per subgroup, which is exactly the detail that tells a reuser what they can compare across conditions. Donor-level demographics are stated for both lines. Held at 4 because within Q15's own fields at_risk_populations and missing_data_documentation are unused, the donor demographics sit in a field outside this question's scope, and there are no inclusion or exclusion criteria in the participant sense because there is no participant cohort. The record also declines to state how many cells were profiled in the Perturb-seq atlas, noting the bundle gives only targeted gene count.

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Persistent URLs for access and documentation
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; external_resources URLs for https://cm4ai.org, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, https://fairscape.github.io, http://integrativemodeling.org; six DOI-identified related datasets.
questions.quality_note: Passes with redundancy. Both a DOI-resolved repository landing page and a project portal are given, so findability does not depend on a single host. All domains are plausible and match the institutions named elsewhere in the record.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met via distribution_formats, access_urls, and a reuse-permitting license.
questions.description: How users obtain the dataset
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path
questions.evidence: distribution_formats notes that all ten files are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse, that individual files below the download size limit may be downloaded directly, and that the Data Access API is available for programmatic access, with the persistentId landing page as access_urls. license_and_use_terms states the CC BY-NC-SA obligations and that commercial use requires separate negotiation. third_party_sharing records that component raw data are deposited in MassIVE, the Sequence Read Archive, and Figshare, and that some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo.
questions.quality_note: Platform, retrieval route, programmatic alternative, and use policy are all specified, and the record additionally warns that the largest image archives may exceed the direct-download limit, which is the practical failure mode a user would otherwise hit. It also discloses the embargo rather than leaving a user to discover missing files. Remaining friction, not enough to move the band: no per-file download_url, and the access route for the embargoed Perturb-seq data is not stated.

questions.name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
questions.description: License clarity, use guidance, social impact analysis
questions.score_label: Very good — full use guidance, generic social impact
questions.evidence: intended_uses gives five categories with usage_notes, including the candid entry that the release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of individual datasets because computed cell maps are not included. prohibited_uses gives two reasons: no clinical decision-making or patient care without regulatory oversight, and no commercial use under CC BY-NC-SA without separate negotiation. discouraged_uses gives two: use without domain expertise, and use as a complete cell-map resource at this interim stage. future_use_impacts has two entries on anticipating applications, integrating them into data governance to optimize benefits and mitigate risks, and an Ethics team suite of tools for ethical, legal, and social ramifications awareness.
questions.quality_note: Use guidance is the strongest part of this record's reusability story: intended, prohibited, and discouraged uses are all populated with reasons, and the guidance is honest about what the release cannot support rather than marketing it. Held at 4 because the social impact half is stated at the level of intent rather than analysis. future_use_impacts describes an ethics programme that will identify and mitigate risks, but names no specific risk of this dataset and no specific mitigation, so there is nothing a reuser could act on or verify.

questions.name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
questions.description: Provenance, derivation, integrity, and quality metadata
questions.score_label: Very good — strong lineage in text, provenance graph referenced not represented
questions.evidence: Integrity: all ten file_collections carry an MD5 checksum and a publication date. Lineage: raw_data_sources names the Krogan and Lundberg laboratory deposition archives as the origins fed to the MuSIC pipeline; raw_sources names four external repository depositions; preprocessing_strategies gives the ordered processing chain; data_collectors attributes each modality to a named laboratory, which supplies the agent side of an entity-activity-agent account. Version lineage: version_access enumerates five releases and related_datasets links all four predecessors by DOI with is_new_version_of. The record states that output data are packaged with provenance graphs using the FAIRSCAPE framework, and cm4ai_release_metadata.zip is described as containing RO-Crate metadata and provenance graphs. Quality: acquisition_methods records was_directly_observed and, for imaging, was_validated_verified with the Human Protein Atlas antibody scoring protocol.
questions.quality_note: Well beyond the version-history-only band: entities, activities, and agents are all identifiable from the text, derivation runs from named archives through named processing stages, and per-file checksums make integrity verifiable. Held at 4 because the actual provenance graph is referenced as living inside a distributed archive rather than represented in the record, and the schema's own derivation slots are unused: was_derived_from and parent_datasets are absent, errata is absent, missing_data_documentation is absent, and no data splits are declared. The lineage a reader can reconstruct is prose, not a graph this record carries.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.applicability_evidence: Bias documentation is not gated by sharing; a dataset that is never released still has documentable biases.
questions.description: Bias taxonomy, categorization, fairness analysis
questions.score_label: Good — one taxonomy-typed bias, no fairness analysis
questions.evidence: known_biases has a single entry: bias_type: representation_bias, described as data derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines that do not represent all biological variants seen in the population at large, with affected_subsets naming all data in the release across MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J and their derivatives. future_use_impacts adds ethics-programme context.
questions.quality_note: The one bias recorded is real, correctly typed against a standard enum value, scoped to affected subsets, and matched by the parallel statement in sampling_strategies.why_not_representative, so it is coherent rather than boilerplate. Held at 3 because the coverage is narrow relative to what the record itself knows. Selection bias from the targeted panel of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes, and measurement bias from antibody-dependent imaging and assay-dependent protein coverage, are both documented in known_limitations and sampling_strategies but never categorized as biases. There are no AIO mappings and no fairness analysis. The gap between two donors, one Black woman with metastatic breast cancer and one healthy Northern European man, and the claim of general applicability is stated but not analyzed.

strengths: Identifier discipline is consistent and mutually corroborating: the DOI prefix, the publisher ROR, and the citation text all independently resolve to the University of Virginia, NIH award numbers validate against NIH structure with the correct institute codes, and cell lines, people, and organizations carry Cellosaurus RRIDs, ORCIDs, and RORs respectively.

Collection protocol is documented at methods-section depth, naming instruments, reagents, immunofluorescence channel assignments, guide-RNA density, and the specific laboratory responsible for each modality.

File enumeration is complete and verifiable: ten archives, each with a name, collection type, compression, displayed size, publication date, and MD5 checksum, matching the stated total_file_count exactly.

Use guidance is unusually candid, with intended, prohibited, and discouraged uses all populated and the intended-use entry openly stating that the release suits per-dataset bioinformatics rather than integrated cell-map analysis because the maps are not included.

The record surfaces source conflicts instead of silently resolving them, naming both the 563 and 464 protein counts and both affiliations for one creator, and stating the ranking rule it applied in each case.

source_caveats does genuine epistemic work, declining to attribute project-level aggregate counts to this specific release, separating a distinct U2OS publication from the CM4AI series, and justifying each of three deliberate omissions by pointing at what the bundle does not state.

Interoperability is declared at every level the schema allows: RO-Crate packaging with FAIRSCAPE provenance, a schema and class the record can be validated against, ontology CURIEs on instances, and typed DOI relationships across the whole release series.
weaknesses: Version numbering is not monotonic. This June 2026 release is version 2.0 while the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases are listed at 2.1, so sorting the series by version misorders it.
The project end date is stated twice and differently: November 2026 in the update plan, and 2026-08-31 in the NIH RePORTER detail under funders.

Preprocessing and annotation tooling document the full cell-map construction pipeline, but the release explicitly excludes predicted cell maps, so the documented processing does not describe what the shipped archives have been through.

Bias documentation records only representation bias, while selection bias from the targeted 200-protein panel and measurement bias from antibody-dependent imaging appear as limitations elsewhere and are never categorized as biases. There is no fairness analysis and no AIO mapping.
No software versions appear for any tool, and GPT-4 in particular is version-sensitive for annotation output; tool URLs sit in external_resources rather than beside the tools they identify.
External repository depositions are named without accession identifiers, so the MassIVE, Sequence Read Archive, and Figshare links cannot be resolved from this record.
File sizes are prose inside descriptions rather than structured byte counts, and the distribution layer names only ZIP and RO-Crate without saying what formats the archives contain.

collection_timeframes, errata, was_derived_from, missing_data_documentation, variables, and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level are all unused; several are justified in source_caveats, but the schema slots that would make the information machine-readable stay empty.
recommendations: Correct the version value so the June 2026 release sorts after the October 2025 release, or add a sentence in version_access explaining the numbering scheme that makes 2.0 the successor of 2.1.
Reconcile the two project end dates, or state explicitly that the NIH award period ends 2026-08-31 while data releases continue to November 2026.

Split the processing documentation into steps applied to the released archives and the downstream cell-map pipeline whose outputs are not in this release, so a reuser can tell what state the files they download are in.

Add selection_bias for the targeted panel of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes and measurement_bias for antibody- and assay-dependent protein coverage, with AIO mappings, and move the incomplete-overlap statement from known_limitations into known_biases as well.
Record version or release identifiers for node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, and the GPT-4 model used by the GSAI pipeline, and attach the repository URL to each tool entry.
Add MassIVE accessions, the NCBI BioProject identifier, and the Figshare DOI to raw_sources and external_resources so the component depositions resolve.
Populate file_collections[].total_bytes with byte counts derived from the displayed sizes, marked as approximate, and name the file formats contained in each archive.
Name a concrete risk of this dataset and its mitigation in future_use_impacts, rather than describing the ethics programme that will produce such analyses.

metadata.independence_note: No file under data/evaluation_llm/ was opened during this evaluation, including for structural or calibration purposes. Scores derive solely from the rubric in the agent definition and the record under evaluation.
